commit.message: feat(safety): plan and verify git mutations

specification.objective: Make GitRex mutations deterministic to plan, guarded against stale observations, and verifiable through shared CLI and TUI operation logic.

requirements.statement: Model each supported mutation with explicit identity, preconditions, expected local and remote effects, network needs, effect and risk classifications, refs, and immutable commit IDs.

Provide side-effect-free dry-run planning for create-branch, switch, cleanup, fetch, pull, and push, showing resolved state, expected effects, risk, immutable IDs, and whether the plan is GitRex analysis or Git-provided dry-run.
Accept expected HEAD, branch, and upstream preconditions, recheck them immediately before mutation, fail closed with PRECONDITION_CHANGED and safe observed state when they differ.
Return structured operation receipts containing identity, changed-state status, relevant before and after identifiers, confirmed effects, and a distinct verification result.

Classify operations as read_only, local_mutation, network_read, remote_mutation, or destructive and expose classification through deterministic CLI capabilities without treating names or generated text as authorization.

After mutations, inspect only affected Git state, verify operation-specific expected effects, report verification failures separately from execution failures, and cover concurrency-sensitive cases with regression tests.
Route CLI and TUI mutations through shared domain/application logic while preserving supported existing behavior and safety checks.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Plans are typed, deterministic for the same observed Git state, adapter-independent, and include refs and immutable IDs when resolvable.
Each named operation supports dry-run; tests show that local refs, index, worktree, and remote refs do not change, and output identifies its dry-run provenance and risk.
A changed expected HEAD, branch, or upstream blocks the mutation with PRECONDITION_CHANGED and safe observed-state details.
Structured receipts distinguish execution, observed effects, and verification; unobservable remote effects are not reported as confirmed.
All five effect/risk classes are explicit and visible in capabilities; operation names and caller-provided descriptions cannot grant authorization.
CLI and TUI use shared operation semantics and retain existing cleanup/reset safeguards and supported interactions.

invariants.statement: Dry-run never mutates local or remote Git state.
Risk classification describes effects but never grants authorization.
A Git command exit code alone cannot produce a verified receipt.

forbidden_states.statement: A stale expected state is ignored and a mutation proceeds.
A receipt claims an effect that was not observed, or a remote effect that Git did not confirm.
A branch name or model-generated text is interpreted as authorization.

inputs.statement: A supported operation and its arguments, optional expected HEAD/branch/upstream values, and dry-run mode.
Current Git state read through the repository-bound Git client.

outputs.statement: A deterministic operation plan or a structured precondition/execution failure.
After execution, a structured receipt containing observed effects and operation-specific verification.

failure_semantics.statement: Expected-state mismatch returns stable code PRECONDITION_CHANGED before invoking the mutation and includes only safe observed state.
Git execution errors and post-operation verification failures use distinct structured error semantics.
Unknown remote outcomes remain unconfirmed in the receipt.
